docs.title: AccelMark Documentation
docs.text:
No single fastest chip — only the best serving recipe for your workload.

AccelMark is an open, reproducible LLM inference benchmark covering 8 Roofline workload suites (A–H) across NVIDIA, AMD, Huawei Ascend, Apple Silicon, Google TPU, Moore Threads, and Iluvatar CoreX.

Run & Submit (~10 min) → Install dependencies, pass the automatic MMLU accuracy gate, and publish your first hardware baseline. Key Findings & Procurement → Explore the 6 empirical regime reversals and the workload-to-recipe decision matrix. Extend AccelMark → Add a new inference engine runner, support a new accelerator family, or query our static JSON API.

docs.text: I want to… Start here Browse live rankings & compare chips Live Leaderboard ↗ Install for NVIDIA, AMD, Ascend, Iluvatar, MTT, TPU, or Mac Installation Submit without using git Submit Without Git (--zip) Reproduce a community run within ±5% Reproduce & Verify Understand Closed vs Open tiers & runner hashing Methodology & Integrity Query the leaderboard locally without a GPU Zero-GPU Advisor & JSON API 阅读中文入门与国内镜像配置 中文快速上手

docs.title: Do I need to tune flags or achieve SOTA speed to submit?
docs.text: No — out-of-the-box reference baselines are the most valuable submissions. AccelMark is designed to measure what practitioners actually get with standard serving recipes, especially on consumer GPUs, older datacenter cards, AMD ROCm, Huawei Ascend, Apple Silicon, Google TPU, Moore Threads, and Iluvatar CoreX.

docs.title: How long does a benchmark run take?
docs.text:
• Pre-flight check (python run.py --init): ~10 seconds, no model download.
  • Suite F (Qwen2.5-0.5B — recommended first run): ~10 minutes on most consumer or datacenter GPUs.
  • Suite A (Llama-3-8B): ~11 minutes on A100-80GB.
  • Suite D / C / B: ~20–22 minutes on A100-80GB.
  • Suite G (Mixtral-8x7B MoE): ~35 minutes on multi-chip nodes.
  • Suite H (Mistral-7B 10K SWA): ~14 minutes on A100-80GB.

Interrupted runs resume automatically when you re-run the same command.

docs.title: I'm behind a firewall / in mainland China — can I use a HuggingFace mirror or local weights?
docs.text: Yes. Two options work out of the box: 1. HF Mirror: Export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com (and HF_TOKEN=... for gated Llama models). 2. Local / air-gapped weights: Copy configs/models_local.yaml.example to configs/models_local.yaml and point each model ID to your local directory, or pass --model-path /path/to/model. AccelMark still records the canonical HuggingFace model ID and revision for apples-to-apples indexing.

docs.title: Why did my fast GPU get 0.00 QPS (SLA FAIL) on Suite A Online?
docs.text: That is expected behavior, not a bug — and one of AccelMark's core empirical findings! The online scenario enforces a strict p99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms latency SLA under Poisson arrivals. On 24–32 GB GPUs (e.g., RTX 4090, RTX 5090), high concurrency saturates the KV cache and pushes queueing latency above 500 ms even when offline throughput exceeds 3,000 tok/s. Submit the result as-is — honest SLA limits are critical data for the community.

docs.title: Can I submit results without using git or opening a PR manually?
docs.text:
Yes! Run: 

python run.py --submit results/community/<run_name> --zip
This validates your files, prints your projected leaderboard rank, and packages a clean .zip bundle you can attach directly to our Result Submission Issue form.

docs.title: What is the difference between community vs verified and reference vs optimized?
docs.text:
• community vs verified (trust tier):
  • community: Passed all automated CI schema, accuracy, and integrity checks.
  • verified: Independently reproduced on the same hardware and runner by another run within ±5%.
  • reference vs optimized vs experimental (runner tier):
  • reference: Standard out-of-the-box engine runner (e.g., nvidia_vllm_47f5d58e, nvidia_sglang_c43a8309).
  • optimized: Performance-tuned or patched runner targeting higher throughput on a specific workload.
  • experimental: Research forks or early previews (e.g., custom quantization/attention kernels).

You can filter by Runner tier on the Results page or locally via python tools/advisor.py --tier reference.

docs.title: Why did CI reject my new runner PR?
docs.text:
The two most common reasons: 1. Hash suffix mismatch: A runner folder must be named {platform}_{customname}_{hash8} where hash8 matches python runners/hash_runner.py runners/<your_folder>/. 2. Vendored upstream source code: CI rejects .vendor/ directories or runner folders with >100 files so the repository stays lightweight. Keep custom framework edits as minimal patches/*.patch files applied via an apply_patches.sh script (see CONTRIBUTING.md#adding-a-new-runner).

Note: You do not need to hand-edit the Supported Platforms table in README.md — maintainers regenerate it periodically.

docs.title: How do I query AccelMark data in my own script or AI agent?
docs.text:
Either fetch the static auth-free JSON endpoints published on GitHub Pages: - https://freedomintelligence.github.io/AccelMark/api/chips.json - https://freedomintelligence.github.io/AccelMark/api/rank.json - https://freedomintelligence.github.io/AccelMark/api/index.json - https://freedomintelligence.github.io/AccelMark/api/suites.json

Or use our zero-GPU CLI advisor locally: 

python tools/advisor.py --suite suite_A --budget 2.0 --tier reference
python tools/advisor.py --engine-compare "A100"
python tools/advisor.py --compare "5090" "4090" "A100" --format markdown

docs.title: Key Empirical Findings
docs.text:
Core thesis: There is no single fastest chip — only the best serving recipe (accelerator, framework, precision, parallelism) for a given workload regime.

This document summarizes the primary empirical takeaways surfaced by AccelMark across its live leaderboard and paper evaluations. Every number below traces back to a pinned runner folder and public result.json artifact under results/.

docs.title: 1. Regime Reversal: Short-Chat Winner Loses Long-Context Prefill
docs.text:
Type I Roofline Reversal (Suite A vs Suite D, same vLLM reference stack):

Accelerator Suite A (Short Chat · ~280 tok in) Suite D (Long Context · ~28K tok in) Suite A Value (tok/$/hr) NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 3,488 tok/s (+29%) 54.3 tok/s (−23%) 4,650 NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB 2,701 tok/s 70.2 tok/s (+29%) 1,800
  • Why it happens: Suite A (Llama-3-8B, ~280-token prompts) is memory-bandwidth bound, where the RTX 5090's high GDDR7 bandwidth shines. Suite D (~28K-token prefill) pushes arithmetic intensity past the roofline knee into a compute-bound regime, where datacenter tensor throughput and sustained prefill execution let A100 pull ahead despite the 5090's peak spec advantage.
  • Practical lesson: Never procure hardware for RAG or long-document summarization using short-prompt decode numbers.

docs.title: 2. Offline Throughput Winner Fails the Production SLA Tier
docs.text:
Type II Capacity & Scheduling Reversal (Suite A, verified vLLM 0.7.3 reference stack):

Accelerator Offline Throughput Online Max Valid QPS (p99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms) NVIDIA H200 (141 GB) 5,731 tok/s (#1 verified) 5 QPS NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 5,128 tok/s 25 QPS (5× higher) NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB) 3,488 tok/s 0 QPS (SLA fail)
  • Why it happens: Two distinct effects decouple offline throughput from production SLA capacity:
  • KV-cache capacity cliff: Under Poisson arrivals, 24–32 GB consumer GPUs run out of KV headroom and queue requests past the 500 ms p99 TTFT budget even when their offline tok/s looks strong.
  • Scheduler batching effect: H200's faster decode lets continuous-batching schedulers pack larger batches per step, pushing prefill/TTFT tail latency past 500 ms earlier than H100 under the same default vLLM scheduler policy.
  • Practical lesson: Always inspect online_max_qps and ttft_p99 alongside offline throughput for interactive services.

docs.title: 3. The Software Stack Can Move a Recipe More Than the Chip
docs.text:
Type II Software-Stack Effect (same physical GPU, swapping only the runner):

Hardware Suite Runner A Runner B Measured Delta NVIDIA H20-3e Suite A (Offline) vLLM 0.7.3 (2,298 tok/s) SGLang 0.5.6 (4,342 tok/s) +89% throughput NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB Suite A (Online SLA) vLLM 0.7.3 (5 QPS) SGLang 0.4.10 / 0.5.6 (100 QPS) 20× SLA capacity NVIDIA A800-SXM4-80GB Suite H (10K SWA) vLLM 0.7.3 (2,069 tok/s) TensorRT-LLM 0.21 (2,316 tok/s) +12% throughput
  • Why it matters: A benchmark that locks one serving engine measures a hardware-software pair, not raw silicon. AccelMark pins every runner by content hash ({platform}_{name}_{hash8}) and surfaces framework filters so readers can separate silicon limits from stack maturity.
  • Check locally: Run python tools/advisor.py --engine-compare "A100" to compare frameworks on any chip with multi-engine submissions.

docs.title: 4. Tensor-Parallel Scaling Inverts Interconnect Generation
docs.text:
Type II Interconnect Amdahl Effect (Suite E · Llama-3-8B, verified vLLM 0.7.3):

Accelerator Interconnect 2× Scaling Efficiency ($\eta_2$) 4× Scaling Efficiency ($\eta_4$) NVIDIA RTX 4090 D PCIe 4.0 94.5% 55.5% NVIDIA H20-3e NVLink 77.2% 54.8% NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB NVLink 3.0 72.5% 47.0% NVIDIA H200 NVLink 4.0 60.2% 32.9%
  • Why it happens: Scaling efficiency $\eta_N = T_N / (N \cdot T_1)$ is governed by the Amdahl ratio of per-die throughput to interconnect bandwidth. H200's per-die decode throughput grew faster than NVLink 4.0 all-reduce bandwidth, so communication consumes a larger fraction of each step than on slower-per-die chips.
  • Practical lesson: For models that fit on 1–2 chips (<70B), prefer data-parallel replicas over wide tensor parallelism (TP > 4).

docs.title: 5. Sparse MoE Rewards Aggregate Bandwidth Over Compute
docs.text:
Suite G (Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, 8-chip multi-GPU):

  • Mixtral activates only 2 of 8 experts per token, keeping arithmetic intensity below dense 8B inference even at 8-chip scale.
  • H20-3e, which trails A100-40GB by ~5% on dense Suite A, beats A100-40GB ×8 by +17% on Suite G (3,757 vs 3,218 tok/s offline) because its aggregate HBM bandwidth becomes the binding resource; H200 ×8 leads verified vLLM runs at 5,334 tok/s.

docs.title: 6. Cost-Efficiency & Quantization Depend on Architecture, Not Labels
docs.text:
• Value Inversion (Suite F, verified vLLM): Tesla T4 achieves 51.3k tok/$/hr — 6.7× higher throughput per rental dollar than H100 (7.6k tok/$/hr). Consumer RTX 4090 D and RTX 5090 routinely deliver 2–3× the tok/$/hr of datacenter GPUs on edge and offline batch workloads.
  • Quantization Path Sensitivity (Suite C):
  • On Hopper / Ada / Blackwell (native FP8 tensor cores), FP8 delivers ~1.5–1.8× speedup while clearing the MMLU accuracy gate.
  • On Ampere (A100/A800/3090), FP8 lacks a native tensor-core path (falling back or emulating), whereas W8A8 (SmoothQuant / INT8) engages native INT8 tensor cores and leads quality-adjusted efficiency (2.30× on RTX 3090, 1.20× on A100).

docs.title: Workload-to-Recipe Decision Matrix
docs.text:
Workload Regime Best-Matched Recipe Weaker Fit (for this regime) Suite Interactive SLA chat H100 80GB · SGLang / vLLM Consumer 24–32 GB GPUs (SLA failure) Suite A Long-context / RAG (28K) B200, H200, H100 H20-3e, RTX 5090 Suite D Offline batch / edge RTX 5090, RTX 4090 D, Tesla T4 Datacenter flagships (cost penalty) Suite F Sparse MoE (Mixtral-8x7B) H200 ×8, H20-3e ×8 Mid-tier compute SKUs, immature TP stacks Suite G Dense <70B scaling Data-parallel replicas Tensor parallelism > 4-way Suite E Quantized serving (Ampere) W8A8 (SmoothQuant) Emulated FP8, W4A16 at high batch Suite C Quantized serving (Ada / Hopper / Blackwell) Native FP8 Unchecked INT4 without MMLU gate Suite C Sliding-window attention (10K ctx) Stack with SWA-aware KV allocation Stacks sizing KV as full attention Suite H

Explore live numbers interactively at freedomintelligence.github.io/AccelMark or locally via python tools/advisor.py.

docs.title: AccelMark Methodology & Protocol
docs.text: AccelMark is designed around a single principle: benchmark complete serving recipes under fixed, auditable contracts — never bare chips under ad-hoc scripts.

docs.title: 1. What Is a Serving Recipe?
docs.text:
A production LLM deployment is defined by four coupled axes:

$$\text{Recipe } h = (\text{accelerator } a,\; \text{serving engine } s,\; \text{precision } q,\; \text{parallelism } p)$$

Changing any single axis — swapping vLLM for SGLang, enabling FP8 vs W8A8, or scaling from TP=1 to TP=8 — can shift throughput or SLA capacity by 20% to 20×. AccelMark records all four axes explicitly in every submission's result.json and env_info.json.

docs.title: 2. Multi-Regime Spectrum Sampling (Suites A–H)
docs.text:
Because inference workloads span from memory-bandwidth bound (low arithmetic intensity, short-prompt decode) to compute bound (high arithmetic intensity, long-context prefill) and communication / capacity bound (multi-chip TP, sparse MoE), no single scalar score preserves hardware rankings.

AccelMark samples eight distinct bottleneck regions:

Suite Bottleneck Region Fixed Model Prompt Shape (in → out) Dataset A Bandwidth decode + online SLA Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct ~280 → ~310 tok sharegpt_standard_v1 B VRAM capacity + multi-chip TP Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct ~280 → ~310 tok sharegpt_standard_v1 C Native quantization vs accuracy Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ~280 → ~310 tok sharegpt_standard_v1 D Compute-bound long prefill Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ~28K → ≤256 tok sharegpt_longctx_v1 E Interconnect Amdahl scaling Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct ~280 → ~310 tok sharegpt_standard_v1 F Single-die bandwidth & tok/$ Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct ~95 → ~150 tok sharegpt_edge_v1 G Sparse MoE routing + agg. HBM Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 ~280 → ~310 tok sharegpt_standard_v1 H Sliding-window KV cache (4K win) Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 ~10K → ≤256 tok sharegpt_swa_v1

Full suite contracts live in suites/suite_*/suite.json and are documented in suites/README.md.

docs.title: 3. Seven Evaluation Scenarios
docs.text:
Each suite selects a required default subset of scenarios and optional extra scenarios:

  1. accuracy (Quality Gate — Always First): Evaluates a pinned MMLU subset on the exact same loaded model instance before throughput runs begin. If accuracy drops beyond accuracy_threshold_delta relative to the BF16 baseline (schema/accuracy_baselines.json), the run aborts (or is permanently flagged if --skip-accuracy-gate is passed).
  2. offline (Peak Throughput): All prompts dispatched concurrently with no SLA constraint; sweeps suite concurrency levels and reports median aggregate tokens/sec across repeated trials.
  3. online (SLA-Bound Capacity): Sweeps Poisson arrival rates (online_qps_levels) and reports max_valid_qps — the highest request rate that maintains p99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms.
  4. interactive (Single-Stream Latency): Concurrency = 1; isolates minimum TTFT and TPOT without queueing contention.
  5. sustained (Thermal & Drift Stability): Fixed concurrency held for 15 min (Suite F) or 30 min (datacenter suites); reports throttle_ratio = min_window_tps / max_window_tps and onset minute.
  6. speculative (Draft-Assisted Decode, extra): Offline decode with a pinned 1B draft model; records speedup and token acceptance rate.
  7. burst (KV-Cache Spike Resilience, extra): Alternates steady baseline traffic with 5× spike windows; reports burst p99 TTFT degradation ratio.

docs.title: Content-Hashed Runner Pinning
docs.text: Every runner lives in runners/{platform}_{name}_{hash8}/, where hash8 is the first 8 hex characters of SHA-256(runner.py) (verified by runners/hash_runner.py). Modifying runner.py requires a new versioned folder with the new hash, ensuring historical leaderboard entries always map 1-to-1 to the exact code that produced them.

docs.title: Runner Tiers
docs.text: To keep apples-to-apples baselines clean while welcoming systems innovation, meta.json tags each runner with runner_tier: - reference (default): Standard, out-of-the-box serving engine integration (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, vllm-rocm, vllm-ascend, vllm-tpu, mlx-lm, vllm-musa, vllm-ixuca). - optimized: Tuned or patched engine variants (must use lightweight patches/*.patch + apply_patches.sh — vendoring upstream trees is blocked by CI). - experimental: Custom research forks or early previews (e.g., turboquant, custom SM70 attention kernels).

docs.title: Deterministic run_id & Automated CI Validation
docs.text: Every submission PR is checked automatically by .github/workflows/validate_pr.yml (runners/validate_submission.py): - Schema validation: Strict checks against schema/result.schema.json and schema/env_info.schema.json. - Deterministic run_id check: Recomputes the SHA-256 identity from hardware, dies_per_card, chip_count, suite_id, implementation_id, precision, and start_time to prevent manual tampering. - Protocol integrity checks: Rejects inverted throughput fields (output_tps > total_tps), zero-token positive throughput claims, missing accuracy baselines, and Suite D truncated-context runs. - No-bloat runner guard: Blocks .vendor/ directories or >100 files inside runner folders.

docs.title: Two-Tier Verification (community → verified)
docs.text:
• community: Any PR that passes automated CI validation lands in results/community/ and immediately appears on the leaderboard with full artifact links.
  • verified: Any independent contributor with matching hardware and runner can rerun the suite (via Reproduction Quests). When the primary metric matches within ±5%, the result is promoted to results/verified/.

docs.title: 5. Agent Optimization Track
docs.text: AccelMark also serves as the trusted black-box evaluator for AccelMark-Agent — evaluating coding agents that optimize real LLM serving stacks under strict anti-gaming controls: - In-place fresh-process baselines - Mandatory MMLU accuracy gates ($\Delta \le 0.03$) - Artifact fingerprinting (unchanged artifacts cannot claim speedups) - 3× independent fresh-process re-measurements - Workload integrity audits (blocking cached responses or edits to protected evaluation configs)

docs.title: First Submission (~10 Minutes)
docs.text:
Audience: Anyone with a single GPU, NPU, TPU, or Mac. Estimated time: ~10 minutes on Suite F (Qwen2.5-0.5B). No tuning required.

No SOTA tuning required

Honest out-of-the-box reference baselines (Closed division) on consumer, older, or emerging accelerators are just as valuable as tuned datacenter runs.

docs.title: Step 1 · Pre-Flight Check
docs.text:
python run.py --init

Expected output:

✓ Submitter profile saved to configs/submitter.yaml (@your-handle)
✓ Detected accelerator: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (24 GB)
✓ Default runner: nvidia_vllm_47f5d58e (reference)

docs.title: Step 2 · Run Suite F (~10 min)
docs.text:
python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_F

--runner auto picks the default reference runner for your detected accelerator (or pass aliases: vllm, sglang, rocm, ascend, iluvatar, musa, tpu, mlx).

What happens automatically:

  1. MMLU Accuracy Gate runs first on the loaded model instance (Δ ≤ 0.03 vs baseline).
  2. Offline + Online + Interactive benchmark scenarios execute under the pinned LoadGen seed.
  3. Results and hardware fingerprints are saved to results/community/<run_dir>/ (result.json + env_info.json).

Pre-Ampere NVIDIA GPUs (V100, T4, RTX 20xx)

Add --enforce-eager if Triton/CUDA-graph compilation fails on older architectures.

docs.title: Step 3 · Validate & Preview Your Rank
docs.text:
python run.py --submit results/community/<run_dir>

Expected output:

✓ Schema validation passed
✓ Protocol & run_id integrity verified
✓ Projected rank on Suite F (Closed): #9 / 34
Next steps:
  git checkout -b submit/<run_dir>
  git add results/community/<run_dir>
  git commit -m "results: add <chip> suite_F"
  git push -u origin submit/<run_dir>

Prefer not to use git? Pass --zip instead and upload on GitHub Issues — see Submit Without Git.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Prerequisites: Python ≥ 3.10, git, and a working accelerator driver / runtime for your platform.

docs.title: 1. Clone & Install Core Harness
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/AccelMark.git
cd AccelMark
pip install -e .

docs.title: 2. Install Runner Dependencies by Platform
docs.text:
NVIDIA (vLLM)NVIDIA (SGLang)AMD ROCmHuawei AscendIluvatar CoreXMoore ThreadsGoogle TPUApple Silicon (MLX) 
pip install -r runners/nvidia_vllm_47f5d58e/requirements.txt

pip install -r runners/nvidia_sglang_c43a8309/requirements.txt

pip install -r runners/amd_vllm_rocm_6c18cd8f/requirements.txt

pip install -r runners/ascend_vllm_ascend_d4aa9fda/requirements.txt

pip install -r runners/iluvatar_vllm_ixuca_4d3befc9/requirements.txt

pip install -r runners/moorethreads_vllm_musa_6607740b/requirements.txt

pip install -r runners/google_vllm_tpu_68cc9ffa/requirements.txt

pip install -r runners/apple_mlx_lm_9546b8b5/requirements.txt

docs.title: 3. Mainland China / Offline Weights (Optional)
docs.text:
If HuggingFace Hub is slow or unreachable in your environment, use either:

# Option A: HuggingFace mirror
export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com

Or map local checkpoints once in configs/models_local.yaml (git-ignored):

Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct: /data/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct: /data/models/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct

docs.title: 4. Verify Setup in 10 Seconds
docs.text:
python run.py --init

This creates your local configs/submitter.yaml handle and verifies hardware detection and runner imports without downloading any model weights. Next: First Submission (~10 min).

docs.title: Add a New Runner or Accelerator Family
docs.text: Every inference engine on AccelMark lives in a self-contained, content-hashed directory under runners/{platform}_{framework}_{hash8}/.

docs.title: 5 Steps to Add a Runner
docs.text:
1. Subclass BenchmarkRunner in runners/<tmp>/runner.py implementing load_model(), generate(), and release_resources().
  2. Compute the content hash (first 8 hex characters of SHA-256 of runner.py): 
    python runners/hash_runner.py runners/<tmp>/runner.py
# → e.g. nvidia_lmdeploy_3f8a2c1d
  3. Rename the folder to match the hash and write meta.json (declare runner_tier: "reference", "optimized", or "experimental", plus supported suites).
  4. Keep it clean (no vendoring): Import upstream packages via requirements.txt — CI rejects PRs that vendor upstream engine source trees.
  5. Validate locally before opening your PR: 
    python runners/validate_runners.py
python run.py --runner <your_folder> --suite suite_F --dry-run

Do not edit README.md

The README platforms matrix is auto-generated from runners/*/meta.json. Maintainers refresh it with python tools/generate_platforms_matrix.py.

For the full subclass API, precision resolution rules, and adding a brand-new hardware platform plugin (collect_env.py), see DEVELOPMENT.md and runners/README.md.

docs.title: Zero-GPU Advisor & Static JSON API
docs.text: You don't need a GPU to use AccelMark data in scripts, procurement sheets, notebooks, or AI agents.

docs.title: 1. Static JSON API (Auth-Free)
docs.text:
Every merge to main publishes static JSON files on GitHub Pages under https://freedomintelligence.github.io/AccelMark/api/:

Endpoint Description api/manifest.json Snapshot version, timestamp, counts, and SHA-256 checksums for all files api/chips.json Indexed accelerators, submission counts, best & median throughput api/index.json Per-chip suite breakdown for fast programmatic lookup api/rank.json Per-submission suite ranks, framework, runner tier, and primary metric api/suites.json Suite specifications, models, and SLA parameters api/schema.json JSON Schema for result.json submissions

docs.title: 2. Local CLI Advisor (tools/advisor.py)
docs.text:
# Best Tok/$ options under $2.00/hr using Closed reference runners
python tools/advisor.py --suite suite_A --budget 2.0 --tier reference

# Compare frameworks (vLLM vs SGLang vs TensorRT-LLM) on the same chip
python tools/advisor.py --engine-compare "A100"

# Export a Markdown or JSON comparison table
python tools/advisor.py --compare "4090" "3090" "A100" --format markdown

docs.title: Multi-Chip & Scaling Guides (Suites B, E, G)
docs.text:
Three AccelMark suites evaluate multi-accelerator setups:

Suite Model Typical Chips What It Measures Suite B Llama-3-70B 4 or 8 chips Large-model VRAM capacity & tensor-parallel serving Suite E Llama-3-8B 1× / 2× / 4× / 8× Linear scaling efficiency & interconnect Amdahl overhead Suite G Mixtral-8x7B ≥2 chips (auto-scaled) Sparse MoE routing & aggregate HBM bandwidth

docs.title: Running Suite B (70B TP)
docs.text:
python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_B --tensor-parallel-size 4
# Or on an 8-chip node:
python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_B --tensor-parallel-size 8

docs.title: Running Suite E (Scaling Sweep)
docs.text:
Suite E automatically sweeps across available chip counts (1, 2, 4, 8) on your node and computes scaling_efficiency_2x, scaling_efficiency_4x, and scaling_efficiency_8x:

python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_E

docs.title: Running Suite G (Sparse MoE)
docs.text:
python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_G --tensor-parallel-size 8

Why does H200 have lower 2× TP efficiency than RTX 4090 D?

Scaling efficiency tracks the ratio of per-die compute throughput to interconnect bandwidth (Amdahl's law). Because H200 finishes each decode step far faster than a 4090 D, all-reduce synchronization consumes a larger fraction of step time — even over NVLink 4.0. For dense models that fit on 1 chip, prefer data-parallel replicas over TP > 4.

docs.title: Reproduce & Verify a Result (±5%)
docs.text: AccelMark's two-tier trust model promotes community submissions to verified once an independent submitter reproduces the measurement within ±5% on matching hardware and runner.

docs.title: 1. Pick an Open Quest
docs.text: Browse Reproduction Quests ↗ and filter by your hardware vendor or suite. Click Copy rerun on any row to copy the exact reproduction command.

docs.title: 2. Run the Reproduction
docs.text:
python run.py --runner <same_runner_folder> \
  --suite <suite_id> \
  --reproduces-run-id <original_run_id> \
  --tier verified

The harness records meta.reproduces_run_id inside your result.json so the leaderboard automatically links both submissions and credits both the original author and the verifier.

docs.title: 3. Submit Your Verification PR
docs.text:
python run.py --submit results/community/<your_run_dir>

Once merged, if the primary metric agrees within ±5%, both entries display the green Verified shield on the leaderboard.

docs.title: Submit Without Git (--zip)
docs.text: Don't want to fork, branch, or use git? Package your validated result into a single .zip archive and upload it through our GitHub Issue Form.

docs.title: 1. Validate & Package
docs.text:
python run.py --submit results/community/<run_dir> --zip

This runs the exact same schema and protocol checks as CI and writes <run_dir>.zip containing result.json and env_info.json.

docs.title: 2. Upload via GitHub Issue
docs.text:
1. Open the Result Submission Issue Form.
  2. Fill in your accelerator model, suite, and runner ID.
  3. Drag and drop the .zip file into the description box and click Submit new issue.

A maintainer will run CI validation and merge your result into the leaderboard with full submitter attribution.

docs.title: run.py — Unified Benchmark Launcher
docs.text: Command Purpose python run.py --init Interactive one-time submitter handle setup & 10-second pre-flight hardware/runner check (no model download) python run.py --list-runners List all installed runners with tier (reference / optimized / experimental) and supported suites python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_F Auto-detect hardware and run the default reference runner on Suite F python run.py --runner <alias_or_id> --suite <suite_id> Run a specific runner (aliases: vllm, sglang, trtllm, rocm, ascend, iluvatar, musa, tpu, mlx) python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_B --tensor-parallel-size 4 Pass multi-GPU tensor parallelism flags through to the runner python run.py --submit results/community/<dir> Validate schema & protocol integrity, preview projected rank, and print exact PR commands python run.py --submit results/community/<dir> --zip Same validation + package a self-contained .zip for no-git GitHub Issue upload

docs.title: tools/advisor.py — Zero-GPU Procurement & Engine Query Tool
docs.text: Command Purpose python tools/advisor.py --suite suite_A --budget 2.0 --tier reference Rank Closed reference recipes under \$2.00/hr by tokens per dollar python tools/advisor.py --engine-compare "A100" Compare all inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, etc.) on the same accelerator python tools/advisor.py --compare "5090" "A100" "H100" --format markdown Export a Markdown or JSON comparison table

docs.title: Validation & Maintenance Scripts
docs.text: Command Purpose python runners/validate_submission.py results/community/<dir> Run exact PR CI checks locally (schema, run_id integrity, sanity bounds) python runners/validate_runners.py Verify all runner SHA-256 folder suffixes & meta.json schemas python tools/generate_platforms_matrix.py --check Check that the README platforms matrix matches runners/*/meta.json python tools/generate_visuals.py Regenerate rank-shift-*.svg, roofline-suites-*.svg, and og-image.png from live leaderboard data

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Consistent terminology used across the AccelMark leaderboard, CLI, paper, and documentation:

Term Definition Serving Recipe A complete, auditable deployment tuple (chip × chip_count × framework × version × precision × parallelism). Every row on AccelMark is a serving recipe, never an uncontextualized chip score. Suite (A–H) A pinned workload contract (model, prompt distribution, token lengths, accuracy baseline, and scenarios) designed to isolate one Roofline bottleneck. Scenario One measurement mode inside a suite (accuracy, offline, online, interactive, sustained, burst, speculative). Runner ({platform}_{name}_{hash8}) A self-contained Python adapter in runners/ whose 8-char suffix is the SHA-256 prefix of runner.py. Closed vs Open Division (Runner Tier) Closed (reference) = default out-of-the-box engine stacks (shown by default on the leaderboard). Open (optimized / experimental) = heavily tuned or custom-kernel forks, cleanly toggleable without contaminating reference baselines. Submission Tier (community → verified) community = CI-validated PR (immediately published). verified = independently reproduced by a second submitter on matching hardware & runner within ±5%. MMLU Accuracy Gate Mandatory 100-question MMLU check run on the exact loaded model instance before throughput benchmarking (Δ ≤ 0.03 vs baseline). SLA Fail Shown on Online QPS when an accelerator cannot sustain even the lowest Poisson arrival rate under the p99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms latency SLA.

docs.title: Workload Suites Reference (A–H)
docs.text: AccelMark uses spectrum sampling across the Roofline model so no single opaque composite score hides real-world hardware reversals.

docs.title: Suite Overview
docs.text: Suite Model Precision Chips Input → Output Default Scenarios Primary Metric Ref Time (A100) A · Single-Chip Chat Meta-Llama-3-8B BF16 1 ~280 → ~310 accuracy, offline, online Offline tok/s & Max QPS ~11 min B · 70B Multi-Chip TP Meta-Llama-3-70B BF16 4 / 8 ~280 → ~310 accuracy, offline, online Offline tok/s ~20 min C · Quantization Llama-3.1-8B BF16 + FP8/W8A8/W8A16/W4A16 1 ~280 → ~310 accuracy, offline (×5) Quality efficiency ~22 min D · 28K Long Context Llama-3.1-8B BF16 1 ~28K → ≤256 accuracy, offline Offline tok/s ~22 min E · Multi-Chip Scaling Meta-Llama-3-8B BF16 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 ~280 → ~310 offline sweep 2× / 4× scaling eff. ~9 min F · Edge / Consumer Qwen2.5-0.5B BF16 / FP16 1 ~95 → ~150 accuracy, offline, interactive Offline tok/s & tok/$/hr ~10 min G · Sparse MoE Mixtral-8x7B BF16 ≥2 ~280 → ~310 accuracy, offline, sustained Sustained / offline tok/s ~35 min H · Sliding Window Mistral-7B BF16 1 ~10K (4K win) → 256 accuracy, offline, online Offline tok/s ~14 min

docs.title: Seven Evaluation Scenarios
docs.text:
• accuracy (mandatory gate): 100-question MMLU subset on the exact loaded model instance (Δ ≤ 0.03).
  • offline: Unbounded batch arrival measuring peak throughput (tokens/sec).
  • online: Poisson arrival sweep reporting highest QPS sustaining p99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms.
  • interactive: Single-stream concurrency=1 TTFT latency (ms).
  • sustained (extra): 15–30 min constant load measuring thermal/fragmentation throttle ratio.
  • burst (extra): Alternating 5× arrival pulses measuring KV admission resilience.
  • speculative (extra): Draft-assisted decoding speedup & acceptance rate.

Full JSON definitions live in suites/suite_*/suite.json.

docs.title: 需要调出 SOTA 极限速度才能提交吗？
docs.text: 完全不需要。 AccelMark 排行榜默认展示的是 Closed（Reference 参考栈），衡量开箱即用、可复现的真实基线。无论是消费级 4090/3090、老卡 V100/T4，还是国产加速卡，诚实的默认跑分都非常有价值。

docs.title: 为什么我很快的显卡在 Suite A Online 上显示 SLA fail（未达 SLA）？
docs.text: Online 场景要求在泊松到达并发下满足 p99 TTFT ≤ 500 ms。24–32 GB 显存的显卡（如 RTX 5090 / 4090）虽然离线吞吐极高，但 KV-Cache 容量与调度队列压力会导致 p99 首字延迟超过 500ms 门槛——这正是 AccelMark 揭示的核心实证发现之一（离线最快 ≠ 生产 SLA 最强），并不是报错。

docs.title: Closed (Reference) vs Open 和 community vs verified 有什么区别？
docs.text:
• Runner 层级（Closed / Open） 区分代码栈：reference 是标准开箱栈（榜单默认显示）；optimized / experimental 是深度魔改或实验内核，可一键切换查看，不会污染标准排名。
  • Submission 信任等级（community → verified） 区分复现度：PR 通过自动 CI 校验即刻以 community 上榜；由另一位贡献者在同硬件、同 Runner 下独立复现且误差 ≤ ±5% 后晋升为 verified（榜单显示绿色盾牌）。

docs.title: 不熟悉 Git / 不想提 PR 怎么提交结果？
docs.text:
在 --submit 命令后加上 --zip：

python run.py --submit results/community/<run_dir> --zip

然后将生成的 .zip 压缩包直接拖拽上传到 GitHub 免 Git 提交表单 即可。

docs.title: 为什么新提交的 Runner PR 会被 CI 拒绝？
docs.text: 常见原因有 3 个：① 文件夹末尾 8 位哈希与 runner.py 的 SHA-256 不一致（运行 python runners/hash_runner.py 核对）；② 仓库内夹带了完整的上游推理框架源码（请改用 requirements.txt 安装）；③ 缺少 meta.json 字段。本地可先运行 python runners/validate_runners.py 自检。

docs.title: 中文快速上手（约 10 分钟）
docs.text: 无需极致调参。 消费级显卡、老卡及国产加速卡（昇腾、天数智芯、摩尔线程等）的诚实默认配置（Closed 参考栈）与数据中心旗舰卡同等珍贵。

docs.title: 1. 克隆并安装核心依赖
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/AccelMark.git
cd AccelMark
pip install -e .

根据你的硬件生态安装对应 Runner 依赖（也可直接在 一屏命令生成器 ↗ 中点选生成）：

  • NVIDIA (vLLM)：pip install -r runners/nvidia_vllm_47f5d58e/requirements.txt
  • NVIDIA (SGLang)：pip install -r runners/nvidia_sglang_c43a8309/requirements.txt
  • 华为昇腾 Ascend：pip install -r runners/ascend_vllm_ascend_d4aa9fda/requirements.txt
  • 天数智芯 Iluvatar：pip install -r runners/iluvatar_vllm_ixuca_4d3befc9/requirements.txt
  • 摩尔线程 MTT：pip install -r runners/moorethreads_vllm_musa_6607740b/requirements.txt
  • AMD ROCm：pip install -r runners/amd_vllm_rocm_6c18cd8f/requirements.txt
  • Apple Silicon：pip install -r runners/apple_mlx_lm_9546b8b5/requirements.txt

docs.title: 2. 中国大陆镜像或本地权重配置
docs.text:
如直连 HuggingFace 较慢，二选一即可：

# 方式 A：使用国内 HuggingFace 镜像
export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com

或 方式 B：在 configs/models_local.yaml（已被 .gitignore 忽略）中映射本地模型目录：

Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct: /data/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct: /data/models/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct

docs.title: 3. 初始化、运行并提交
docs.text:
# 10 秒初始化署名与环境预检（不下载模型）
python run.py --init

# 跑最快的 Suite F（单卡约 10 分钟，自动先过 MMLU 精度门禁）
python run.py --runner auto --suite suite_F

# 校验并预览预计排名（不想用 git 可加 --zip 打包后通过 GitHub Issue 表单上传）
python run.py --submit results/community/<run_dir>

遇到问题请查阅 中文常见问题 FAQ。
